PricingPage.metadata-description: Compare Nakafa Free and Pro for learning materials, practice questions, Nina AI tutoring, and online Tryouts.
PricingPage.drink-note: The difference is that this one lasts a whole month.
PricingPage.drink-idr: {count, plural, one {iced milk coffee} other {iced milk coffees}}
PricingPage.per-day-note-idr: Roughly the price of one motorbike parking.
PricingPage.per-day-note-other: Roughly the monthly price divided by 30.
PricingPage.q6: Can I learn without an account?
PricingPage.a6: Yes. Public lessons can be read without an account. You need to sign in to save your progress, ask Nina and take practice tests.
PricingPage.a9: Nina uses credits when she answers your question. One answer uses {cost} credits.
PricingPage.a10: Free credits renew every day. Pro credits renew at the start of every month.
PricingPage.q11: Do unused credits carry over to the next period?
PricingPage.a11: No. Unused credits expire when a new period starts.
PricingPage.q12: What happens when I run out of credits?
PricingPage.a12: Nina can be used again after the next credit renewal, or once you move to Pro. Lessons and practice questions stay available.
PricingPage.q13: Do failed Nina answers still use credits?
PricingPage.a13: No. If Nina cannot finish an answer, no credits are taken.
PricingPage.a14: Yes. Sign in before you pay so that Pro connects to your Nakafa account. Pro stays active until you cancel it.
PricingPage.q15: How do I manage or cancel Pro?
PricingPage.a15: Sign in to your account, choose the Pro button, then manage or cancel the subscription in the customer portal.
PricingPage.a16: Your account goes back to the Free plan and receives the daily Free credits.
PricingPage.q17: Will the basic lessons stay free?
PricingPage.q20: Can I use Nakafa on my phone?
PricingPage.a20: Yes. Nakafa works in a browser on phones, tablets, and computers without installing an app.

Faq.q4: What subjects and grades do you cover?
Faq.a4: We cover K-12 through university. Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry, Biology, Computer Science, and more. From elementary basics to advanced university courses.
Faq.q7: How does Nakafa ensure content accuracy?
Faq.a7: All content is created by qualified contributors and reviewed by the community. Our source-available approach means anyone can inspect materials and propose improvements. Practice exercises include explanations so you learn from mistakes, not just scores.

Landing.nina-chat-answer:
### 13 comes from taking m as 3

That gives $5(2) + 9/3 = 13$. The trouble is that $m = 3$ does not fit the question.

#### Check it against what you know

$\triangle(2, 4) = 2(2) + 4/3 \neq 8$

With $m = 1$ it fits: $2(2) + 4/1 = 8$. So $m$ must be 1, and the answer is 19.
